ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a purple quadrilateral, and a pink dashed diagonal connects the lower-left vertex to the upper-right vertex, dividing the quadrilateral into two triangles. The upper side of the upper triangle is labeled 6 m, and the perpendicular dashed height from the lower-left vertex to this upper side is labeled 17 m. The base of the lower/right triangle is labeled 28 m, and the perpendicular dashed height from the upper-right vertex to the base is labeled 15 m. Then reason: The area of the quadrilateral equals the sum of the areas of the two triangles. Area of the upper triangle = 1/2 × 6 × 17 = 51. Area of the lower triangle = 1/2 × 28 × 15 = 210. Total area = 51 + 210 = 261.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the purple quadrilateral is split by the dashed diagonal from the lower-left vertex to the upper-right vertex into two triangles. The upper-left triangle has a side labeled 6 m, and the dashed perpendicular from the opposite lower-left vertex to that side is labeled 17 m. The lower-right triangle has base 28 m along the bottom, and the dashed perpendicular from the upper-right vertex to that base is labeled 15 m. Compute the two triangle areas separately: upper triangle area = (1/2)(6)(17), lower triangle area = (1/2)(28)(15). Add them to get the total area: 51 + 210 = 261.

method.method_draft: Label the vertices around the quadrilateral as A = upper-left, B = upper-right, C = lower-right, and D = lower-left. From the diagram, AB = 6 m and the perpendicular distance from D to line AB is 17 m, so area(△ABD) = (1/2)(6)(17).
